CoreWeave 上季營收較去年同期增加 112% 至 25.8 億美元，跑贏市場所預測的 25.6 億美元。淨損 6.26 億美元，高於去年同期的 2.9 億美元，當時每股虧損 60 美分，經調整後每股虧損 1.03 美元，優於市場所估的虧損 1.2 美元。
該公司目前未完成訂單 (backlog) 已跨越 1000 億美元整數關卡，達 1040 億美元，而且這還沒算進本季新增逾 250 億美元的承諾。此外，目前已啟用的電力容量達 1.5GW。
展望方面，CoreWeave 預估第 3 季營收將介於 34-36 億美元，以區間中值計算，相當於年增率將達 158%。
CoreWeave 目前預估 2026 年調整後營業利益為 9.6-11.5 億美元，營收 124-132 億美元，優於該公司 5 月時預估的調整後營業利益 9-11 億美元，以及營收 120-130 億美元。
此外，今年底啟用電力容量將超過 1.85GW，全年資本支出預估為 350 億至 390 億美元，高於 5 月時預估的 310 億至 350 億美元。

成立八年的 CoreWeave 正與雲端市場龍頭亞馬遜 (AMZN-US)、Google(GOOGL-US) 及微軟 (MSFT-US) 競逐資料中心建設，這些資料中心配備可運行生成式人工智慧 (Gen AI) 模型的晶片。然而不同於上述業者，CoreWeave 目前仍未實現獲利：截至上季末，其資產負債表上的負債達 350 億美元，主要用於支應採購輝達 (NVDA-US) 圖形處理器 (GPU) 及其他設備的成本。

全美各地監管反彈

美國各地近來對資料中心建設的反對聲浪升高，例如紐約州州長 Kathy Hochul 便在 7 月簽署行政命令，宣布暫停新建大型資料中心。
CoreWeave 執行長 Mike Intrator 在財報電話會議中表示：「當我們和各位討論這些數字時，我們是根據目前的進展，以及我們在這裡給出的財測來衡量。就目前而言，這些數字都不會受到監管反彈的影響。」
不過，反對聲浪仍對公司構成挑戰。Intrator 說：「毫無疑問，當美國部分地區甚至不願意參與相關討論時，事情就會變得更加困難。」
執行長 Intrator 表示，CoreWeave 在租用輝達晶片方面看到有利趨勢。他說：「我們 Blackwell 及 Vera Rubin 系列產品的價格與利潤率均創下新高，而前幾代產品的價格則維持在多年前的水準或更高。」
財務長 Nitin Agrawal 表示，公司已將零組件價格上漲的成本轉嫁給客戶。
CoreWeave 上季獲得 Meta Platforms(META-US) 宣布追加 210 億美元支出，另外還宣布與 Anthropic 簽訂多年期協議，並取得量化交易公司 Jane Street 承諾的 60 億美元訂單。
與此同時，市場競爭正在升溫。SpaceX(SPCX-US) 已開始出售多餘的運算容量，Meta 也考慮推出雲端業務。
財務長 Agrawal 說：「即使競爭加劇，我們仍看到需求、價格及利潤率同步擴張，這顯示 CoreWeave 產品及整體業務仍具成長空間，而我們所處的總可服務市場 (TAM) 本身已經非常龐大。」

items.title: 輝達5000億美元AI融資計畫啟動 受惠股一次看
paras: 輝達 (NVDA-US) 計畫攜手 Apollo、貝萊德、黑石、Brookfield、高盛與 KKR，共同動員逾 5,000 億美元第三方資本，為 AI 資料中心及算力基礎設施提供融資。這項計畫若順利落地，可能改變 AI 資料中心的建設與融資模式，但目前的合作承諾並不等同資金已實際投入。
從整體架構來看，輝達可望成為最大策略受益者。這家 AI 巨頭不僅能藉由外部資金擴大 GPU 市場需求，也可將主要融資與違約風險交由私人資本承擔，降低自身資產負債表的壓力。
受惠程度分析：

最直接受惠：輝達、CoreWeave、Nebius
 融資業務受惠：Apollo、貝萊德、黑石、Brookfield、高盛、KKR
 潛在供應鏈受惠：美光、Sandisk、Coherent、Lumentum、Credo、康寧、Applied Optoelectronics


過去部分合作模式中，輝達除了供應 GPU，也可能透過融資承諾或擔保協助客戶取得資金，引發市場質疑公司是否正在為自身產品需求提供資金，形成「循環融資」。
美銀分析師 Vivek Arya 指出，在新架構下，相關債務主要由私人資本聯盟承擔。輝達負責維持 GPU 設備及算力的資產價值，但不直接為融資債務提供擔保，因而可把市場對 GPU 快速折舊的疑慮，轉化為推動 AI 基礎設施融資的條件。
美銀估計，輝達過去的供應商融資曝險，約相當於公司 2026 年與 2027 年預估自由現金流 4,700 億美元的 15%。若更多融資需求轉由第三方資本承擔，輝達便能保留更多現金，用於股票回購或其他策略性投資。
市場目前預估，輝達 2026 年可能回購約 730 億美元股票，2027 年進一步增至 1,060 億美元，約占同期自由現金流 36% 至 37%，仍低於公司承諾返還股東逾五成自由現金流的目標。
富國銀行分析師 Aaron Rakers 認為，輝達的角色已不再只是晶片供應商，而是開始參與 AI 基礎設施的建設與融資設計。透過將 GPU 算力標準化，並轉化為可出租、可交易及可投資的資產，輝達正協助市場建立新的「AI 工廠」投資類別。
CUDA 軟體生態系也有助延長 GPU 的實際使用週期，並讓算力在不同營運商之間調度，進而維持設備出租收益並降低折舊壓力。美銀預估，全球 AI 系統市場規模到 2030 年可能達到 1.7 兆美元，輝達可望占有 65% 至 70% 市占率。
除了輝達，新雲端運算業者 CoreWeave (CRWV-US) 與 Nebius (NBIS-US) 也可望成為直接受益者。
這類業者需要投入大量資金採購 GPU 及興建資料中心，但由於信用評等未達投資等級，借貸成本通常高於大型科技公司。若私人資本能提供規模更大、成本更低的融資，便可減輕業者的資本支出與現金流壓力。
彭博行業研究分析師 Vasu Kasibhotla 指出，更充裕的資金可協助 CoreWeave 執行龐大的資本支出計畫，也能強化 Nebius 擴張所需的財務基礎。業者因此有機會更快取得稀缺的電力與資料中心據點，同時降低透過增發股票籌資造成的股權稀釋。
不過，目前尚未確認 CoreWeave 或 Nebius 已從這項 5,000 億美元計畫取得資金，相關影響仍取決於後續融資安排與實際投入規模。
參與合作的六大金融機構也可能成為主要受益者。Apollo (APO-US)、貝萊德 (BLK-US)、黑石 (BX-US)、Brookfield (BAM-US)、高盛 (GS-US) 與 KKR (KKR-US)，可藉此建立大型 AI 基礎設施投資平台。
這些業者可將 AI 資料中心設計成由實體設備擔保、並與算力使用收入連結的信貸資產，吸引退休基金、保險公司及其他機構投資人投入。對私人資本業者而言，AI 資料中心有機會成為繼能源、交通與不動產後，另一項可大規模配置的基礎設施資產。
若 5,000 億美元資金最終轉化為資料中心建設，記憶體與光通訊供應鏈也可能間接受惠。不過，目前尚未出現新的訂單數據或企業財測支持這項推論，因此仍屬方向性的潛在利多。
在記憶體領域，美光 (MU-US) 可望受惠於高頻寬記憶體 (HBM) 需求增長；Sandisk (SNDK-US) 則可能受益於企業級固態硬碟需求擴大。資料中心建設若加速，將有助維持記憶體供應吃緊的格局，並支撐產品平均售價。
隨著 AI 叢集規模擴大至數十萬顆晶片，傳統銅線逐漸面臨傳輸距離與速度限制，也將推升高速光纖與光子元件需求。
Coherent (COHR-US) 與 Lumentum (LITE-US) 供應 800G 及 1.6T 網路使用的高速雷射與光收發模組；Credo (CRDO-US) 提供機櫃連接所需的主動式電纜與數位訊號處理晶片；康寧 (GLW-US) 供應高密度光纖；Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI-US) 則可能受惠於雲端業者增加光收發模組採購。
儘管市場對這項合作抱持期待，5,000 億美元仍是計畫動員的資金規模，而不是已部署的資本。金融機構是否真正投入資金，仍取決於能否找到信用良好、且有能力持續支付算力費用的終端客戶。
另一項風險是，充裕融資可能只是讓企業提前採購 GPU，未必代表 AI 基礎設施的長期需求同步增加。若實際算力使用率不如預期，設備殘值、貸款品質及最終損失承擔者都可能成為市場關注焦點。
資金也無法解決電力短缺、土地取得、電網連接與地方監管等實體限制。即使資料中心獲得融資，仍可能因供電不足或審批問題而延後甚至取消。
此外，融資架構愈複雜，投資人愈難判斷 AI 建設背後的真實債務風險。如果市場無法清楚辨識資金來源、擔保責任與設備殘值，相關公司的估值也可能承受壓力。
市場接下來將聚焦輝達 8 月 26 日公布的 2027 會計年度第二季財報。投資人將關注輝達在融資平台中的具體責任、公司仍保留多少供應商融資曝險，以及釋放現金流後是否會進一步擴大股票回購。

items.title: AI資產化遇最大考驗！輝達5000億美元融資恐遭中國晶片狙擊
items.title_en: AI Assetization Faces Its Biggest Test! Nvidia’s $500 Billion Financing May Be Targeted by Chinese Chipmakers
paras: 輝達 (NVDA-US) 創辦人暨執行長黃仁勳正試圖為 AI 產業建立一套全新的融資模式，將 GPU 與資料中心視為類似商用不動產、倉儲或收費公路等可以用來借貸的生產性資產。不過，這項規模高達 5000 億美元的 AI 融資計畫正面臨一項關鍵風險，即中國 AI 晶片產業快速擴張，若未來中國以低價晶片搶占市場，可能導致 GPU 價格與抵押品價值快速下滑，進而威脅華爾街投入的大筆資金。
輝達近期宣布與全球 6 大資產管理及金融機構達成協議，包括貝萊德 (BLK-US)、黑石(BX-US)、阿波羅全球管理(APO-US)、KKR(KKR-US)、布魯克菲爾德資產管理(BAM-US) 及高盛(GS-US)，目標是建立規模達 5000 億美元的第三方融資資金池，用於協助缺乏足夠現金或信用評級的企業建設資料中心、AI 運算叢集並採購 GPU。
黃仁勳表示，輝達的 AI 工廠平台已經是一種「可投資資產」及「基礎設施資產」，原因在於這些運算設備能夠生產價值、創造收入，而且具有可替代性，同時被幾乎所有主要雲端服務供應商採用，並可以運行各種 AI 模型。
這項構想的核心，是改變金融市場對 GPU 的傳統認知。
在傳統資產抵押融資中，銀行願意提供貸款，主要是因為借款人違約後，銀行可以收回建築物、倉庫或貨輪等資產，再透過成熟的二級市場出售並收回部分資金。這類實體資產通常可以使用數十年，而且市場對其殘值具有較明確的判斷。
但最新一代 GPU 究竟能維持多少年的經濟價值，目前仍存在高度不確定性。
隨著新一代 AI 晶片不斷推出，最新 GPU 通常優先用於前沿 AI 模型訓練，但幾年後可能逐漸轉向利潤率較低的 AI 推論工作。這種使用場景的轉換可能直接影響 GPU 的二手價格、租賃收益以及作為貸款抵押品的價值。
FedWatch Advisors 創辦人 Ben Emons 表示，折舊是這項融資模式面臨的關鍵風險。他指出，輝達晶片的折舊速度可能比市場預期更快，一旦如此，GPU 就很難像商用不動產一樣維持長期且穩定的抵押價值。
而 Emons 認為，這項計畫最大的潛在威脅可能來自中國。
中國正快速擴大本土 AI 運算能力，如果中國晶片製造商持續提高產量，甚至透過低價策略向全球市場輸出晶片，可能引發 AI 硬體價格戰。若大量低成本中國晶片進入市場，輝達 GPU 的價格可能快速下降，進而導致數千億美元私人貸款背後的抵押品價值縮水。
對金融機構而言，問題在於 GPU 的價格可能在貸款期限內快速下跌。若抵押品貶值速度快於貸款本金下降速度，一旦借款人違約，投資人即使收回 GPU，也可能無法透過出售二手晶片彌補貸款損失。
因此，Emons 估計，投資人可能不會按照房地產等長期資產的方式為 GPU 提供低成本融資，而是把 GPU 視為高折舊設備，要求更高的報酬率。他估計，視投資人在資本結構中的順位不同，相關資產可能需要 11% 至 17% 的高收益率才能吸引資金。
另一項風險則來自借款人的信用品質。
根據美銀證券分析，這類融資的潛在借款人可能包括無法進入傳統債券市場的非投資級企業，其中包括 AI 新創公司與「新雲」業者。這些企業雖然需要大量 GPU 建立運算能力，但本身可能缺乏足夠的資產負債表實力。
如果這類高風險借款人最終無法償還債務，華爾街資產管理公司就可能被迫接管 GPU，再將使用過的晶片重新出售。但如果屆時市場正處於晶片價格下跌周期，金融機構可能面臨抵押品價值不足的問題。
不過，中國因素短期內仍不太可能立即衝擊輝達的融資模式。
目前中國 AI 晶片市場仍受到美國出口管制影響。中國主要 AI 晶片供應商華為自 2019 年起便被美國商務部列入實體清單。美國政府今年 5 月更表示，華為 Ascend 系列 AI 晶片涉及違反美國出口管制規定，進一步限制美國企業使用相關晶片。
在此背景下，輝達目前仍是美國 AI 晶片市場的絕對領導者。按照多數市場估計，輝達目前在美國 AI 晶片市場的市占率超過 75%。
而且目前 GPU 需求與租賃市場仍對黃仁勳有利。
隨著超大規模雲端業者積極擴建 AI 資料中心，市場對 GPU 運算能力的需求仍然強勁。黃仁勳指出，輝達 H100 GPU 的租賃價格已從 2025 年底每 GPU 每小時約 1.70 美元，上升至今年約 2.35 美元，顯示高階 AI 運算能力仍處於供不應求狀態。
這種高租賃價格也是輝達試圖將 GPU 金融資產化的重要依據。
如果 GPU 可以持續被租賃並產生現金流，那麼金融機構就不必只依靠晶片的二手殘值評估其價值，而可以根據 GPU 未來產生的收入能力進行融資。這與商用不動產依靠租金收入支撐資產價值的邏輯相當類似。
輝達另一項重要護城河則是 CUDA 軟體生態系。
CUDA 是輝達打造的軟體平台，可讓開發者在其 GPU 上運行 AI 及其他高效能運算工作負載。輝達認為，CUDA 持續更新與優化，可以讓既有硬體在部署後維持較高的運算效率，使舊款 GPU 即使不再適合最前沿的 AI 模型訓練，仍能在推論及其他工作負載中繼續產生收入。
換言之，輝達的金融化構想並不完全建立在「GPU 本身能使用多久」，而是建立在「GPU 在整個軟硬體生態系中能持續產生多少現金流」。
這也成為 5000 億美元融資計畫能否成功的核心問題。
如果 AI 模型需求持續快速增加，GPU 租賃價格維持高位，新一代晶片推出後舊 GPU 仍能轉向推論市場，金融機構便可能將 AI 運算設備視為具有長期收益能力的基礎設施，進一步降低 AI 企業取得資本的門檻。
但如果中國 AI 晶片產能快速增加，低價硬體大舉進入市場，或者新一代 GPU 性能提升速度遠超預期，使舊晶片快速失去經濟價值，輝達的折舊速度就可能大幅提高。屆時，金融機構面對的將不再是穩定產生租金的不動產，而可能是一批迅速貶值的高科技設備。
因此，黃仁勳目前的賭注不只是輝達下一代晶片能否繼續領先，也包括 AI 運算設備能否從快速折舊的電子產品，轉變成可以支撐數千億美元債務的長期生產性資產。
對輝達而言，這項計畫若成功，將可能把 AI 基礎設施融資推向全新的市場規模，讓更多 AI 新創企業、雲端服務商及企業客戶在不大幅占用自身資產負債表的情況下取得 GPU 與資料中心資金。
但對華爾街投資人而言，5000 億美元的背後同樣代表一項巨大的抵押品風險。未來 AI 需求、GPU 租賃價格、晶片折舊速度，以及中國 AI 硬體的產能與價格策略，都可能決定這場 AI 金融化實驗最終會成為新的基礎設施融資模式，還是一場規模龐大的資產價格豪賭。
paras_en: Nvidia (NVDA-US) founder and CEO Jensen Huang is trying to create a brand‑new financing model for the AI industry, treating GPUs and data centers like commercial real estate, warehouses, or toll roads that can be used as productive assets for borrowing. However, this $500 billion AI financing plan faces a key risk: China’s AI chip industry is expanding rapidly, and if China later captures the market with low‑priced chips, GPU prices and collateral values could plunge, threatening the massive capital Wall Street is putting into the scheme.

Nvidia recently announced agreements with six global asset‑management and financial firms—BlackRock (BLK‑US), Blackstone (BX‑US), Apollo Global Management (APO‑US), KKR (KKR‑US), Brookfield Asset Management (BAM‑US) and Goldman Sachs (GS‑US)—to create a $500 billion third‑party financing pool to help companies lacking cash or credit ratings build data centers, AI compute clusters and purchase GPUs.

Huang said Nvidia’s AI factory platform is already an “investable asset” and an “infrastructure asset” because the compute equipment can generate value, create revenue, is interchangeable, is used by almost all major cloud providers, and can run a variety of AI models.
The core of the idea is to change the financial market’s traditional view of GPUs.

In conventional asset‑backed lending, banks are willing to lend because, if the borrower defaults, they can seize buildings, warehouses or ships and sell them in mature secondary markets to recover part of the loan. These physical assets typically have decades of usable life, and the market has a fairly clear sense of their residual value.
But how many years the latest‑generation GPUs can retain economic value remains highly uncertain.

As new AI chips are launched, the newest GPUs are first used for cutting‑edge AI model training, but after a few years they may shift to lower‑margin inference work. This shift can directly affect second‑hand GPU prices, leasing yields and the value of GPUs as loan collateral.

Ben Emons, founder of FedWatch Advisors, said depreciation is the key risk for this financing model. He noted that Nvidia chips could depreciate faster than the market expects, making it hard for GPUs to maintain a long‑term, stable collateral value like commercial real estate.
Emons believes the biggest potential threat to the plan could come from China.

China is rapidly expanding its domestic AI compute capacity. If Chinese chip makers keep raising output and even export chips at low prices globally, an AI hardware price war could erupt. A flood of cheap Chinese chips could drive Nvidia GPU prices down sharply, shrinking the collateral value behind tens of billions of private loans.

For lenders, the problem is that GPU prices could fall quickly during the loan term. If collateral values decline faster than the loan principal, lenders may recover the GPUs after a default but be unable to recoup the loss by selling the used chips.

Thus Emons estimates investors may not provide low‑cost financing for GPUs the way they do for long‑term assets like real estate, but will treat GPUs as high‑depreciation equipment and demand higher returns. Depending on the investor’s position in the capital structure, the assets could need an 11%‑17% high‑yield rate to attract capital.
Another risk comes from the credit quality of borrowers.

Bank of America securities analysts say potential borrowers for this type of financing could include non‑investment‑grade companies that cannot access traditional bond markets, such as AI startups and “new‑cloud” providers. These firms need large numbers of GPUs to build compute capacity but may lack strong balance‑sheet strength.

If these high‑risk borrowers ultimately cannot repay, Wall Street asset managers may be forced to take possession of the GPUs and resell the used chips. But if the market is in a chip‑price‑decline cycle at that time, financial institutions could face insufficient collateral value.
However, the China factor is unlikely to hit Nvidia’s financing model in the short term.

China’s AI chip market is still constrained by U.S. export controls. China’s main AI chip supplier Huawei has been on the U.S. Commerce Department’s entity list since 2019. In May this year the U.S. further stated that Huawei’s Ascend AI chips violate export regulations, further restricting U.S. firms from using those chips.
Against this backdrop, Nvidia remains the outright leader in the U.S. AI chip market. Most estimates put Nvidia’s share of the U.S. AI chip market at over 75%.
And current GPU demand and leasing markets still favor Huang.

As hyperscale cloud providers aggressively expand AI data centers, demand for GPU compute power remains strong. Huang noted that the leasing price for Nvidia’s H100 GPU has risen from about $1.70 per GPU per hour at the end of 2025 to roughly $2.35 this year, showing that high‑end AI compute capacity is still in short supply.
This high leasing price is a key justification for Nvidia’s push to financialize GPUs.

If GPUs can continue to be leased and generate cash flow, lenders need not rely solely on the chips’ second‑hand residual value to assess worth; they can finance based on the future income the GPUs will produce. This logic mirrors how commercial real estate values are supported by rental income.
Another important moat for Nvidia is its CUDA software ecosystem.

CUDA is Nvidia’s software platform that lets developers run AI and other high‑performance workloads on its GPUs. Nvidia believes that ongoing updates and optimizations to CUDA keep existing hardware efficient after deployment, allowing older GPUs to continue generating revenue in inference and other workloads even when they’re no longer suited for cutting‑edge model training.

In other words, Nvidia’s financialization concept does not rest entirely on “how long a GPU can be used,” but on “how much cash flow a GPU can keep generating within the broader hardware‑software ecosystem.”
That question is at the heart of whether the $500 billion financing plan can succeed.

If AI model demand keeps growing rapidly, GPU leasing prices stay high, and older GPUs can shift to the inference market after new generations launch, lenders may view AI compute equipment as long‑term revenue‑producing infrastructure, further lowering the capital barrier for AI firms.

But if China’s AI chip capacity expands quickly, low‑cost hardware floods the market, or the performance leap of new GPUs far outpaces expectations—making older chips lose economic value fast—Nvidia’s depreciation rate could spike dramatically. Lenders would then be dealing not with stable, rent‑producing real estate but with rapidly devaluing high‑tech equipment.

Thus Huang’s bet is not only on Nvidia’s next‑generation chips staying ahead, but also on AI compute equipment transforming from fast‑depreciating electronics into long‑term productive assets that can back tens of billions of dollars of debt.

For Nvidia, if the plan works it could push AI infrastructure financing into a completely new market size, allowing more AI startups, cloud providers and corporate customers to obtain GPU and data‑center funding without heavily loading their own balance sheets.

But for Wall Street investors, the $500 billion also represents a huge collateral risk. Future AI demand, GPU leasing rates, chip depreciation speed, and China’s AI‑hardware capacity and pricing strategy will all determine whether this AI financialization experiment becomes a new infrastructure‑financing model or a massive asset‑price gamble.

items.title: 〈財報〉AI需求強！美超微獲利大勝預期 盤後飆8%
items.title_en: Earnings Report: AI Demand Soars! Super Micro Computer Beats Expectations with 8% Stock Price Surge
paras: AI 伺服器製造商美超微電腦 (Super Micro Computer)(SMCI-US) 周二 (11 日) 公布 2026 會計年度第四季財報，受人工智慧 (AI) 需求加速帶動，獲利遠高於華爾街預期，激勵盤後股價一度大漲 8%。
美超微公布，第四季調整後每股盈餘 (EPS) 為 1.70 美元，營收 111 億美元。FactSet 調查的分析師原本預期，每股盈餘為 0.92 美元、營收 116 億美元。
相比之下，美超微去年同期每股盈餘為 0.41 美元，營收 58 億美元。

Q4 財報關鍵數據 v.s. FactSet 預估


營收：111 億美元 v.s. 116 億美元
調整後 EPS：1.70 美元 v.s. 0.92 美元


執行長梁見後在財報新聞稿中表示，「過去一年，我們新增了數百家企業及其他客戶，取得超過 600 億美元的新訂單，並以創紀錄的積壓訂單進入 2027 會計年度。」
他指出，「隨著需求加速，我們透過提高企業客戶占比，以及更廣泛採用完善的資料中心建構組件解決方案 (Data Center Building Block Solutions, DCBBS) 架構，持續改善獲利能力。」
公司同時表示，第四季毛利率為 17.6%。此前美超微於 7 月 21 日公布第四季初步財務結果時，預估第四季毛利率將介於 15% 至 17%。
隨著各企業積極建置支撐 AI 所需的基礎設施，美超微伺服器的需求大幅增加。由於需求強勁，美超微具備定價能力，有助於提升利潤率。
這項需求預計短期內不會放緩。美超微預期第一季營收將介於 145 億至 155 億美元，相較去年同期的 50.2 億美元，將成長 189% 至 209%，也高於分析師預估的 118 億美元。

FY 2027 Q1 財測 v.s. FactSet 預估


營收：145-155 億美元 v.s. 118 億美元
 EPS：1.01-1.10 美元 v.s. 0.72 美元


公司並預期第一季調整後每股盈餘將介於 1.01 至 1.10 美元，也優於市場原先預期的 0.72 美元。
2027 會計年度營收預計介於 650 億至 720 億美元，華爾街目前預估為 530 億美元。
paras_en: Super Micro Computer (SMCI-US), a manufacturer of AI servers, released its Q4 2026 financial report on Tuesday, with profits far exceeding Wall Street expectations due to accelerating AI demand, leading to an 8% stock price surge after hours.
Super Micro Computer reported Q4 adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.70 and revenue of $1.11 billion, surpassing FactSet's analyst expectations of $0.92 EPS and $1.16 billion in revenue.
In comparison, Super Micro Computer's EPS was $0.41 and revenue was $580 million in the same period last year.
Key Q4 financial data vs. FactSet estimates: Revenue: $1.11 billion vs. $1.16 billion, Adjusted EPS: $1.70 vs. $0.92.

CEO Charles Liang stated in the earnings press release, 'Over the past year, we added hundreds of new customers and secured over $60 billion in new orders, entering the 2027 fiscal year with a record backlog.'

He noted, 'As demand accelerates, we continue to improve profitability by increasing our enterprise customer mix and adopting our Data Center Building Block Solutions (DCBBS) architecture more broadly.'
The company reported a Q4 gross margin of 17.6%, which was within the 15% to 17% range estimated on July 21 when preliminary Q4 financial results were announced.

As companies actively build infrastructure to support AI, demand for Super Micro Computer's servers has increased significantly, allowing the company to raise prices and boost profit margins due to strong demand.

This demand is expected to continue in the short term, with Super Micro Computer forecasting Q1 revenue of $1.45 billion to $1.55 billion, representing a 189% to 209% increase from $502 million in the same period last year, and exceeding analyst estimates of $1.18 billion.
The company also expects Q1 adjusted EPS to be between $1.01 and $1.10, outperforming the market's original expectation of $0.72.

items.title: AI下一波投資機會曝！分析人士：「這些」AI「收費企業」將是真正贏家
paras: 人工智慧（AI）投資熱潮持續延燒，但市場觀察人士指出，投資人若想掌握下一波真正的獲利機會，應減少聚焦於已經上漲的標的，轉而思考十八個月後市場可能熱議的題材。分析人士並以記憶體類股為例，說明市場往往在趨勢明朗前忽視真正的機會所在。
《MarketWatch》報導指出，2025 年初本波 AI 行情剛啟動時，市場資金幾乎全數集中於輝達 (NVDA-US) 、圖形處理器（GPU）及資料中心相關供應鏈。
相較之下，記憶體產業則普遍被視為典型的景氣循環類股，過去屢次讓投資人受挫，鮮少受到青睞。
然而，事後發展顯示，此一判斷付出了不小代價。短短十八個月內，記憶體從乏人問津的冷門族群，躍升為 AI 供應鏈中最關鍵的瓶頸產業之一。
蘋果 (AAPL-US) 執行長庫克（Tim Cook）曾以「百年一遇的洪水」形容記憶體缺貨的嚴峻程度。在股價上，SanDisk (SNDKV-US) 與美光科技 (MU-US) 同期漲幅則雙雙超過十倍。
分析人士指出，這項案例的啟示不僅限於記憶體產業本身，真正優異的投資機會，事前往往並不明顯。
例如，能源類股在 2022 年大漲前並不受市場青睞；比特幣與貴金屬在 2023、2024 年走強之前同樣乏人問津；記憶體產業在 AI 改寫供需結構前，也一度被視為過時的景氣循環股。
分析人士強調，一旦股價已充分反映趨勢確立的訊號，其實已錯過主要漲幅。

AI 基礎建設熱潮 與網路泡沫本質不同

市場近期高度關注科技巨頭在 AI 領域的鉅額資本支出。
根據美國銀行 (BAC-US) 預估，微軟 (MSFT-US) 、亞馬遜 (AMZN-US) 、Alphabet(GOOGL-US) 、Meta(META-US) 與甲骨文 (ORCL-US) 未來兩年將在晶片、伺服器、網路設備、電力、散熱系統及資料中心等項目投入逾 2 兆美元，龐大金額也引發外界將其與 2000 年前後的網路泡沫相提並論。
不過，分析人士認為，此一類比忽略了關鍵差異。
1990 年代末期，電信業者係依據對未來網路需求的預測，大舉興建基礎設施；世界通訊（WorldCom）、環球電訊（Global Crossing）與奎斯特國際通訊（Qwest）等公司斥資鋪設光纖網路與資料中心，賭注在於需求終將到位。
然而，基礎設施擴張速度遠超實際客戶需求，泡沫破滅後，產業留下大量閒置的「暗光纖」，導致價格崩跌，重債電信業者相繼倒閉。
分析人士表示，當前的 AI 基礎建設熱潮情況不同。微軟、亞馬遜、Alphabet 與甲骨文並非基於需求「預期」而擴建產能，而是客戶已提前數年預訂運算容量，部分相關設施甚至尚未完工，訂單即已排定。

訂單數據支撐需求已現

上述論點亦反映在各公司最新財報數據上：

微軟公布的未履行商業訂單餘額達 6270 億美元，較去年同期近乎倍增，平均合約期限約 2.5 年；
Alphabet 旗下 Google Cloud 訂單積壓金額達 2400 億美元，同樣較去年同期成長逾一倍，既有客戶消耗雲端服務的速度更較原始合約承諾快逾 30%；
亞馬遜雲端運算服務（AWS）則寫下疫情高峰以來最快成長速度，其 AI 業務與客製化晶片業務年化營收規模雙雙突破 250 億美元。


分析人士指出，兩者的核心差異在於：1990 年代末的電信業擴建，是「先建置、再等待客戶上門」；而本波 AI 基礎建設，很大程度上屬於「客戶已在排隊等候」的性質。
儘管市場近期仍因鉅額資本支出計畫，對相關企業股價祭出賣壓，但分析人士預期，這樣的態勢可能於未來十八個月內出現反轉。
屆時，市場有望重新評價能從 AI 運算需求中持續收取「費用」，即所謂的「AI 收費企業」的價值。

潛在受惠標的：雲端巨頭與晶片供應鏈中介者

分析人士認為，若上述論點成立，真正的受惠者將是憑藉 AI 工作負載賺取經常性收入的企業，而非單純供應硬體設備的廠商。
其中，亞馬遜就被視為指標性的「純收費」型企業，無論企業訓練模型、部署 AI 代理或進行推論運算，均須透過其雲端服務並支付費用。
Alphabet 同樣具備類似優勢，Google Cloud 業務成長快速、訂單積壓持續擴大，AI 亦逐步為其搜尋、雲端及企業軟體業務創造更多營收。
微軟則被視為掌握此一題材品質最高的標的之一，其 Azure 雲端平台位居企業導入 AI 的核心位置，並可透過雲端基礎設施、Office 辦公軟體及整體軟體生態系統將 AI 服務變現。
分析人士並指出，上述三家企業市值雖均已達兆美元規模，且其 AI 業務成長速度，可能於未來數年大幅提升其整體獲利能力，若此情境成真，現階段的估值水準或未如市場認知般偏高。
總的來說，下一波真正的投資機會，可能就藏在「誰將於 AI 基礎建設完工後持續收費」此一問題的答案之中。

items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉美元持平 市場靜待CPI數據
paras: 美元周二 (11 日) 持平，外匯市場參與者在攸關貨幣政策前景的重要通膨數據公布前保持觀望。油價則小幅上漲，此前一名伊朗官員表示，在美國滿足德黑蘭提出的要求之前，荷姆茲海峽 (Strait of Hormuz) 將持續關閉。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數 (DXY) 幾乎沒有變化，報 99.82。
市場目前將目光聚焦周三及周四公布的美國 7 月消費者物價指數 (CPI) 及生產者物價指數 (PPI)。這些數據繼上周五公布的就業報告之後登場，該報告意外疲弱，導致市場大幅重新調整對聯準會(Fed) 升息的預期。
經濟學家預期，7 月整體 CPI 及核心 CPI 月增率將分別高於 6 月的負成長及持平表現。以年增率來看，兩項指標預計都將較 6 月小幅放緩。
Interactive Brokers 資深經濟學家 José Torres 表示，「如果明日核心通膨略低於預期、來到 2.4%，可能創下 63 個月來的新低，這正凸顯地緣政治緊張局勢如何掩蓋成本壓力正在降溫的情況。」
他指出，「事實上，整體 CPI 預計將比扣除食品及能源價格的版本高出近 1%，這項巨大的差距顯示，如果川普總統能促成一項持久的中東和平協議，將可能帶來顯著的去通膨進展。」
Torres 補充，「在我看來，一旦這場爭端獲得解決，升息很快就會不再是市場討論的議題，因為聯準會 2% 的通膨目標將在年底前觸手可及，政策焦點也將迅速轉向避免勞動市場進一步惡化。」
伊朗：美國須滿足要求 荷姆茲海峽才會重新開放
目光轉向中東，油價周二上漲近 2%，此前一個交易日已大漲 5%。
自上周以來，交易員一直關注荷姆茲海峽重新開放是否會達成某種協議。這是因為包括美國總統川普在內的美國官員一再表示，雙方正在進行談判。但伊朗否認這些說法，並表示目前只與阿曼接觸，沒有與華盛頓進行任何直接談判。
雙方對這條重要水道的狀況說法不一。美方堅稱荷姆茲海峽已對商業航運開放，伊朗則警告，該海峽實際上處於關閉狀態。雙方說法不一，加上和平協議遲遲沒有突破，推升了近幾個交易日的油價。
伊朗一直與阿曼就建立荷姆茲海峽管理框架進行討論。卡達外交部發言人表示，兩國談判已進入後期階段，並處於關鍵轉折點。
同時，《彭博社》引述巴基斯坦國防部長 Khawaja Muhammad Asif 報導，美國與伊朗正接近就潛在和平協議達成「某種安排」。阿曼及巴基斯坦一直是目前這場衝突的主要調停者。
伊朗要求，荷姆茲海峽重新開放的前提是美國必須滿足 6 月達成、但後來破裂的臨時和平協議中所列條件，包括解除美國海上封鎖、撤銷制裁，以及賠償戰爭造成的損失。美國總統川普周一回擊提出自己的賠償要求。
根據 Kpler，通過荷姆茲海峽的航運量降至極低水準。航運追蹤數據顯示，獲確認通過海峽的船隻數量，從上周五的 15 艘降至周六的 11 艘，周日只有 6 艘。
日元回吐更多干預後漲幅
其他主要貨幣方面，日元周二兌美元小幅走弱，進一步回吐上個月歷史性干預後取得的部分漲幅。

items.title: 〈台幣〉區間整理收32.278元 貶值4.7分
items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Trades in Narrow Range, Falls 4.7 Points to NT$32.278
paras: 新台幣今 (11) 日升貶互見，午盤過後趨貶，終場收在 32.278 元，貶值 4.7 分，台北外匯經紀公司成交值 14.22 億美元。
新台幣今日以 32.25 元、貶值 1.9 分開出後，最高來到 32.174 元，明顯緩和日前一度靠攏 32.5 元關卡的壓力，而午盤過後轉貶，最低見 32.302 元，低於昨日的低點，反映匯市處在區間整理，全日高低價差 1.28 角。
觀察主要亞幣，以泰銖相對較弱貶值約 0.5%，新台幣收貶 0.15%，星元貶近 0.1%，人民幣、日元小貶不到 0.05%，韓元則小幅升值 0.05% 上下。
法人分析，美國非農就業人口意外減少 2.3 萬人，且 5-6 月就業人數較先前公布值減少 10.3 萬人，且若排除疫情期間，勞動參與率已降到 1970 年代以來最低水準，薪資年增率也寫下 5 年新低，顯示美國勞動市場放緩趨勢超乎預期，短線有利升息預期降溫，接下來觀察本周將公布的 7 月 CPI 數據。
paras_en: The Taiwan dollar traded in a narrow range today, fluctuating between NT$32.25 and NT$32.174 before falling to NT$32.278 at the close, down 4.7 points from the previous day. The total turnover was NT$142.2 billion, according to the Taipei Foreign Exchange Association.

The Taiwan dollar opened at NT$32.25, down 1.9 points from the previous day's close, and reached a high of NT$32.174 before falling to a low of NT$32.302, below yesterday's low. The price range was NT$1.28, indicating a period of consolidation in the foreign exchange market.

Among major Asian currencies, the Thai baht was the weakest, falling by about 0.5%, while the Taiwan dollar fell by 0.15%, and the Singapore dollar fell by nearly 0.1%. The Chinese yuan and Japanese yen fell by less than 0.05%, while the Korean won rose by 0.05%.

Analysts said that the unexpected decline in the US non-farm employment population by 23,000 people, and the reduction of 103,000 jobs in May and June from the previously announced figures, indicate that the US labor market is slowing down more than expected. This trend is likely to reduce the likelihood of interest rate hikes in the short term, and investors will be watching the release of the July CPI data next week.

items.title: 美日聯合干預成效消退！市場聚焦日本央行升息與套利風險 日元反彈幅度回吐近半
items.title_en: Japan's Intervention Effect Fades as Market Focus Shifts to BOJ Rate Hike and Carry Trade Risk
paras: 外匯市場最新數據顯示，美日罕見聯手進場干預匯市帶來的日元升幅正快速蒸發。
日元兌美元匯率上月底貶至 164 附近、創 40 年新低後，美日協同買入日元一度將匯價推回 155 水準，但短短數週反彈幅度已經回吐近一半。
美元周一 (10 日) 走弱令日元回升至 159.36，隔日小幅反彈又讓日元回落至 159.08 附近，顯示干預買盤難敵利差與資金流向的基本面壓力。
美國商品期貨交易委員會 (CFTC) 最新持倉數據顯示，槓桿基金仍握有日元淨空頭，僅在干預後略為縮減。
羅素投資全球解決方案策略主管 Van Luu 說：「干預效果正在消退，要讓日元持續走強，必須有貨幣政策配套。」
目前，市場共識逐漸清晰，在日本央行 (BOJ) 不跟進緊縮的前提下，單靠日本財務省砸錢阻貶只買得到時間，但買不到趨勢。
焦點因此轉向 BOJ。雖然上月會議決議維持 1% 利率不變，但會議摘要與紀錄均釋出偏鷹訊號，有委員稱核心通膨率逼近 2%、「升息節奏恐快過市場預期」。
交易員目前押注 9 月升息 1 碼機率約 50%，高盛與花旗更預估 BOJ 自 9 月起加速升息，明年底基準利率恐將升至 2%。
然而，利差仍是壓倒性「重力」。BOJ 即便升息至 2%，仍遠低於美國聯邦基金區間，套利交易邏輯依舊，倉位就難大規模平倉。
摩根大通首席日本經濟學家藤田綾子認為，短期利差縮小仍不足以扭轉結構，「只有日本長天期殖利率逐步向海外靠攏，套利規模才會實質萎縮」，那是中長期工程。
令交易員警惕的是，當前局面與 2024 年 8 月「黑色星期一」前有幾分神似：日元處弱勢區間、空頭倉位偏大、日銀臨加息窗口、美國數據若轉軟便可能觸發「聯準會轉鴿＋日銀轉鷹」的快速重定價，屆時日元急升、套息盤集中回補，或重演全球風險資產劇烈波動。但多家機構也提醒，這次頭寸槓桿與集中度較當年溫和，聯準會若有序降息，未必複製極端踩踏。
若日元再破 160——這個曾數度觸發日本單邊干預的紅線——輸入型通脹將再加壓，華府亦會憂心日本動用巨額美債儲備擴大干預、反噬美債市場。換言之，8.45 兆日圓單日干預的昂貴地板暫時守住了底線，卻沒寫出新趨勢；接下來數週的美國 CPI、零售數據與日銀 9 月會議，才是決定日元是否只是「反彈一半」、還是「回原點」的真正裁判。
paras_en: The latest data from the foreign exchange market shows that the rapid depreciation of the yen, which was triggered by the rare joint intervention by the US and Japan, is quickly eroding.

The yen, which had fallen to around 164 at the end of last month, a 40-year low, was briefly pushed back to around 155 by the joint buying of the US and Japan, but the rebound has already retreated by nearly half in just a few weeks.

The dollar weakened on Monday (10th) and the yen rose to 159.36, and the next day it fell to around 159.08, showing that the intervention buying power is struggling to overcome the fundamental pressure of interest rate differentials and capital flows.
The latest data from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) shows that leveraged funds are still net short on the yen, with only a slight reduction after the intervention.
Russell Investments' Global Solutions Strategy Head Van Luu said, 'The intervention effect is fading, and to keep the yen strong, there must be monetary policy support.'

Currently, the market consensus is becoming clear, and under the premise that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) will not follow the tightening, relying solely on the Ministry of Finance's money to block the depreciation will only buy time, but not the trend.

The focus has therefore shifted to the BOJ. Although the last month's meeting decided to maintain the 1% interest rate unchanged, the meeting summary and records both released hawkish signals, with some committee members saying that the core inflation rate is approaching 2% and 'the pace of interest rate hikes may be faster than market expectations.'

Traders are currently betting on a 50% chance of a 1-point rate hike in September, with Goldman Sachs and Citi predicting that the BOJ will accelerate interest rate hikes from September, with the benchmark interest rate potentially reaching 2% by the end of next year.

However, the interest rate differential remains the 'gravity' that is overwhelming. Even if the BOJ raises interest rates to 2%, it is still far below the US Federal Funds rate range, and the logic of carry trade still holds, making it difficult to scale back positions.

Morgan Stanley's chief Japan economist, Ayako Sera, believes that the short-term narrowing of interest rate differentials is still insufficient to reverse the trend, 'Only when Japan's long-term interest rates gradually converge with overseas rates will the scale of carry trade shrink', which is a medium-term project.

What is worrying traders is that the current situation is similar to the 'Black Monday' in August 2024: the yen is in a weak zone, the short position is large, the BOJ is approaching the interest rate hike window, and if US data turns soft, it may trigger a rapid re-pricing of 'Fed dovish + BOJ hawkish', leading to a sharp rise in the yen, a concentrated carry trade, or a repeat of the global risk asset volatility. However, several institutions also remind that this time the leverage and concentration are milder than last year, and if the Fed has a orderly rate cut, it may not replicate the extreme stampede.

If the yen breaks through 160 again, which has triggered Japan's unilateral intervention several times, it will put more pressure on Japan's import-pushing inflation, and the US will also worry about Japan using its massive US Treasury holdings to expand intervention, which will backfire on the US Treasury market. In other words, the expensive floor of 8.45 trillion yen per day has temporarily held the line, but has not written a new trend; it is only in the next few weeks' US CPI, retail sales data, and the BOJ's September meeting that will be the true judges of whether the yen is just 'rebounding by half' or 'returning to zero'.

據經濟觀察家調查，日本 7 月服務業景氣判斷指數升至 45.7，但日本首相高市政府的擴張性財政支出計畫推高債券收益率，讓人擔憂 BOJ 的任何緊縮政策舉措都可能被支撐債券市場的政治壓力升高所抵消，引發日圓賣壓，並據美國公布 7 月就業趨勢指數升至 107.71，而且伊朗重申只有在美國滿足包括賠償、解除制裁及停止軍事威脅等條件後，才會重新開放荷姆茲海峽，中東地緣政治局勢持續緊張，激發對美元的避險買盤，兌日圓上漲至 159.36 高點。預估今日美元兌日圓支撐於 158.70-90，阻力於 159.70-90。

items.title_en: Japan and US Joint Intervention Fails to Stem Yen's Decline
paras: 日元由升轉貶，回吐了半數美國和日本歷史性聯手幹預激發的漲幅。
日元週一 (10 日) 收盤走貶，兌美元下跌 1% 至 159.29 日元，成為當日 G10 貨幣中表現最弱的幣別。此次跌勢抹去日元近期干預行情約一半漲幅，對仍密切關注官方是否進一步出手的交易員而言，這是一個具有重要心理意義的轉折。
State Street 策略師李費里奇（Lee Ferridge）表示，如果沒有新的干預措施，日元將持續走弱。市場似乎對當局沒有採取更多干預措施感到失望。
在月初前後，美日兩國聯手展開了自 1998 年以來首次的聯合買匯阻貶行動，助推日元自近 40 年低點反彈。該貨幣在 7 月下旬曾一度走弱至約 164 日元兌 1 美元，隨後在 8 月初的聯合支撐下飆升至 155 日元的高峰。
在月初前後，美日兩國聯手展開了自 1998 年以來首次的聯合買匯阻貶行動，助推日元自近 40 年低點反彈。該貨幣在 7 月下旬曾一度走弱至約 164 日元兌 1 美元，隨後在 8 月初的聯合支撐下飆升至 155 日元的高峰。
不過，日元此後再度陷入疲弱，市場焦點重新回到影響匯率的基本面因素。美日之間巨大的利差、日本財政前景疑慮，以及地緣政治不確定性，持續對日元形成壓力。儘管東京與華府官員均警告，若有需要將再次採取行動。
高盛集團策略師特里維迪（Kamakshya Trivedi）等人在報告中指出：「我們認為，干預後市場反應相對有限，反映出日元走弱背後仍存在基本面因素。」他們預期，「除非全球環境出現轉變，或政策出現意外調整，日元貶值壓力將隨時間重新浮現。」
這波反轉凸顯出，在推動日元下跌的核心力量大致完好無缺之際，干預措施在扭轉日元整體走勢上仍有其侷限性。這也引發了市場臆測，認為當局可能會再度出手支撐匯率。
部分投資人擔心，由於日本週二適逢假日，市場流動性低於平日，可能創造有利於進一步干預的環境。野村證券策略師後藤裕二郎（Yujiro Goto）等人在報告中表示，市場參與者正密切關注官方表態，「焦點仍將集中於日本與美國當局對匯市干預的立場。」
美國銀行外匯策略師亞歷克斯・柯恩（Alex Cohen）認為，若要推動日元進一步升值，需要更「強力」的干預措施，或日本央行釋出將在 9 月升息的訊號。
彭博市場策略師布蘭登・費根（Brendan Fagan）認為，日元干預可以清理槓桿並重新設定匯率，但若沒有實質性的利差收斂，或市場波動大幅升高以降低套利交易吸引力，導致日元走弱的因素仍然存在。
日本央行 7 月底召開利率會議時維持利率不變，但總裁植田和男在會後記者會上釋出偏鷹派訊號，強調物價前景的上行風險增加。該次會議意見摘要也顯示，多名官員指出通膨風險正在升高，其中一名理事更提到，升息速度可能加快。
市場目前預期日本央行 9 月升息機率約為 63%，而 10 月升息幾乎已完全反映在價格中。
Pioneer Investments 策略師帕瑞什・烏帕迪亞（Paresh Upadhyaya）表示：「除非伴隨更強有力的政策行動，否則我對日元大幅升值持懷疑態度。9 月升息本身並不足以支撐日元走強。」
paras_en: The yen has reversed its earlier gains and plummeted 1% to 159.29 against the US dollar on Monday, becoming the worst-performing currency among the G10 currencies.
The decline erased nearly half of the yen's recent gains following the joint intervention by the US and Japan, which has left traders wondering if the authorities will take further action.

State Street strategist Lee Ferridge said that if there are no new intervention measures, the yen will continue to weaken. The market seems to be disappointed that the authorities have not taken further action.

In the early part of the month, the US and Japan jointly launched a joint buying of yen to block its decline, which helped the currency rebound from its 40-year low. The yen had briefly weakened to around 164 yen per dollar in late July, but then surged to a high of 155 yen per dollar in early August after the joint support.

However, the yen has since fallen into weakness again, and the market has shifted its focus back to the fundamental factors that affect the exchange rate. The huge interest rate differential between the US and Japan, Japan's fiscal concerns, and geopolitical uncertainty have continued to put pressure on the yen.

Despite Tokyo and Washington officials warning that they would take action if necessary, the yen has continued to weaken. Goldman Sachs strategist Kamakshya Trivedi and others in a report said that the market reaction to the intervention has been relatively limited, reflecting the underlying fundamental factors driving the yen's decline.
They expect that unless there is a change in the global environment or an unexpected policy adjustment, the yen's depreciation pressure will reappear over time.
This reversal highlights the limitations of intervention in reversing the yen's overall trend, and has sparked market speculation that the authorities may take further action to support the currency.

Some investors are concerned that the Japanese market will be closed on Tuesday, which could create a favorable environment for further intervention. Nomura Securities strategist Yujiro Goto and others in a report said that market participants are closely watching the authorities' stance on intervention, and that the focus will remain on the Japanese and US authorities' positions on currency intervention.

US Bank's foreign exchange strategist Alex Cohen said that to push the yen further higher, more 'forceful' intervention measures are needed, or the Bank of Japan needs to signal that it will raise interest rates in September.

Bloomberg's market strategist Brendan Fagan said that yen intervention can help to clean up leverage and reset the exchange rate, but if there is no significant narrowing of interest rate differentials or a significant increase in market volatility to reduce the attractiveness of arbitrage trades, the factors driving the yen's decline will still exist.

The Bank of Japan maintained its interest rate unchanged at its July meeting, but Governor Haruhiko Kuroda signaled a hawkish bias in a press conference, emphasizing the increasing risk of inflation. The meeting's summary also showed that several officials pointed out that the risk of inflation is rising, with one director even suggesting that the pace of interest rate hikes could accelerate.
The market currently expects a 63% probability of a September interest rate hike by the Bank of Japan, and a near-complete reflection of the price in the October interest rate hike.

Pioneer Investments strategist Paresh Upadhyaya said, 'Unless accompanied by more robust policy actions, I remain skeptical about a significant appreciation of the yen. A September interest rate hike alone is not enough to support the yen's strength.'

paras: 美元周一 (10 日) 自連續兩周跌勢反彈，油價持續走高帶動避險需求，為美元提供支撐。外匯市場參與者同時在消化 7 月就業報告弱於預期後，市場對聯準會 (Fed) 升息預期的快速重新調整，目前將目光轉向本周稍晚公布的重要通膨數據，以進一步尋找利率走向的線索。另一方面，日元兌美元周一貶值近 1%，回吐上月歷史性聯合外匯干預後的部分漲幅。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數 (DXY) 上漲 0.3%，報 99.82。過去兩周累計下跌近 2%。
油價周一上漲近 5%，因伊朗排除與美國直接談判的可能性，並表示只有在華盛頓滿足特定條件後，才可能全面重新開放荷姆茲海峽 (Strait of Hormuz)。此外，伊朗支持的葉門青年運動 (Houthi) 攻擊沙烏地阿拉伯能源基礎設施，也進一步加劇市場對區域石油運輸的擔憂。在此背景下，交易員轉向具避險特性的美元。
伊朗國營媒體報導，議會委員會已批准相關管理框架，其中包括禁止敵對船隻通行的條款。伊朗外交部發言人 Esmaeil Baqaei 周一表示，伊朗與阿曼尚未完成有關海峽管理的聯合聲明，並補充稱，相關計畫將包括監控船隻通行的機制，並應為此取得補償。
伊朗也排除與美國進行直接談判的可能性，聲稱美方違反 6 月達成的臨時和平協議。德黑蘭再次提出全面重新開放荷姆茲海峽的條件，包括結束美國海上封鎖、解除制裁，以及就戰爭造成的損失進行賠償。
川普周一表示，伊朗要求賠償自 2 月底美國與以色列對德黑蘭發動聯合攻擊以來所造成的損失。川普表示，他也將「要求伊朗賠償」，並已指示代表「務必將這點納入未來任何談判之中」。
通膨數據成市場焦點
把目光從中東局勢移開，美元周五下跌 0.4%，因數據顯示，美國非農就業人口 2 月以來首次單月下降，主要受到地方政府教育相關職缺減少的影響。此外，5 月和 6 月的非農就業人口合計遭下修 10.3 萬人。
這份就業報告讓聯準會的政策前景更加複雜。一方面，儘管最新數據表現不佳，整體勞動市場仍穩健。另一方面，由於伊朗戰爭導致油價持續波動，通膨風險大幅升高，而部分聯準會決策官員在 7 月最近一次貨幣政策會議上已明顯傾向升息。
交易員在就業數據公布後，下調了對聯準會 9 月升息的預期。
Northwestern Mutual Wealth Management 投資長 Brent Schutte 表示，「7 月勞動市場報告疲弱的好處是，這可能讓政策制定者有更多空間維持利率不變。過去幾年，我們一再看到聯準會偏重其雙重使命中的就業面向，因此，儘管通膨仍偏高，但在最近兩次勞動市場數據略顯疲弱的情況下，聯準會在進一步升息問題上採取審慎態度，也不令人意外。」
目前市場焦點已轉向本周公布的重要通膨指標，以尋找更多貨幣政策走向的線索。重頭戲將是周三與周四分別公布的 7 月消費者物價指數 (CPI) 及生產者物價指數 (PPI)，接著周五還將公布 7 月零售銷售數據。

Against this backdrop, traders turned to the dollar, which is viewed as a safe‑haven asset.

Iranian state media reported that a parliamentary committee has approved a related management framework that includes a clause banning hostile vessels from transiting the strait. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said on Monday that Iran and Oman have not yet completed a joint statement on strait management and added that the plan will include a mechanism to monitor ship passages and will seek compensation for it.

Iran also dismissed the possibility of direct negotiations with the United States, claiming the U.S. violated the temporary peace agreement reached in June. Tehran reiterated its conditions for a full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, which include ending the U.S. naval blockade, lifting sanctions, and receiving compensation for war‑related damages.

Former President Trump said on Monday that Iran is demanding compensation for losses incurred since the joint U.S.–Israeli attack on Tehran at the end of February. Trump said he would also "demand compensation from Iran" and has instructed his representatives to "make sure this point is included in any future negotiations."
Inflation data become the market’s focus.

Turning away from the Middle‑East backdrop, the dollar fell 0.4% on Friday after data showed that U.S. non‑farm payrolls declined for the first time in a month since February, mainly due to fewer local‑government education jobs. In addition, the May and June non‑farm payroll figures were revised down by a total of 103,000 jobs.

The employment report adds complexity to the Fed’s policy outlook. On the one hand, despite the weak latest data, the overall labor market remains robust. On the other hand, oil‑price volatility caused by the Iran conflict has sharply raised inflation risks, and some Fed officials already showed a clear inclination toward a rate hike at the July monetary‑policy meeting.
Traders lowered their expectations for a Fed rate hike in September after the employment numbers were released.

"The upside of a weak July labor‑market report is that it may give policymakers more room to keep rates unchanged," said Brent Schutte, chief investment officer at Northwestern Mutual Wealth Management. "In recent years we have repeatedly seen the Fed prioritize the employment side of its dual mandate, so even though inflation remains elevated, it is not surprising that the Fed is taking a cautious stance on further hikes after two slightly weaker labor‑market releases."

Market attention has now shifted to this week’s key inflation indicators for more clues on monetary policy direction. The headline events will be the July Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI) released on Wednesday and Thursday, followed by July retail‑sales data on Friday.
The yen gives back more of the gains made after the intervention.

The yen weakened sharply on Monday, with the dollar/yen rising 0.9% to 159.26. The yen has now erased part of the appreciation it gained after last month’s historic joint intervention, the first coordinated yen‑buying action by the U.S. and Japan since 2011.

Before the intervention, the yen had fallen to 164 per dollar, a 40‑year low. Continued yen depreciation would pressure Japan’s import‑dependent economy. To support the yen, Japanese authorities typically sell U.S. Treasury bonds—Japan is the largest single foreign holder of U.S. debt—and use the proceeds to buy yen.
Japanese financial markets were closed on Tuesday for a national holiday.
Among other major currencies, the euro slipped 0.1% against the dollar to $1.1541 per euro.
The pound rose 0.1% against the dollar to $1.3507 per pound.

items.title: 日元干預效果遞減 8月表現為G10貨幣最差 市場靜待日銀下步行動
items.title_en: Yen Intervention Effect Fades, August Performance Worst Among G10 Currencies
paras: 日元匯率在經歷了 7 月的強勁反彈後，8 月份再度陷入疲軟。儘管日本與美國近期聯手進行了自 1998 年以來的首次協同干預，但隨著干預效應消退，日元本月表現遜於所有 G10 成員國。
根據數據顯示，日元兌美元匯率在 8 月已下跌約 0.9%，部分回吐了 7 月份約 3.2% 的漲幅。此前美日當局在日元貶至近 164 的四十年低點後出手，一度將匯率推升至 155 附近，但目前已回落至 158.85。
據分析，日本當局在 7 月 30 日與 31 日分別斥資約 530 億及 340 億美元進行干預，若 7 月 30 日的數據獲得證實，將創下史上最大單日干預紀錄。
高盛與野村證券的分析師指出，日元持續承壓的主因在於美日間巨大的利差、對日本財政支出的擔憂以及地緣政治的不確定性。即使東京與華盛頓官方警告準備再次行動，分析師認為若全球環境或政策未出現重大轉向，日元貶值壓力恐將持續存在。
此外，日本銀行 7 月會議意見摘要顯示，通膨風險正在升溫，甚至有委員提議加速升息。目前換匯市場預期 9 月升息的機率約 63%，而 10 月升息則幾乎被完全定價。
由於目前適逢日本盂蘭盆節假期，市場參與度降低且流動性變薄，交易員正密切警惕當局是否會利用此時機再次出手干預。
paras_en: The yen has weakened in August after a strong rebound in July, despite Japan and the US conducting their first joint intervention since 1998. The intervention effect has worn off, and the yen's performance this month has been the worst among all G10 member countries.

Data shows the yen has fallen about 0.9% against the dollar in August, partly reversing the 3.2% gain in July. The intervention had pushed the exchange rate up to around 155, but it has since fallen back to 158.85. The authorities intervened after the yen hit a 40-year low of nearly 164.

Analysts say Japan intervened on July 30 and 31, spending around $53 billion and $34 billion, respectively. If the July 30 data is confirmed, it would set a record for the largest single-day intervention in history.

Analysts at Goldman Sachs and Nomura Securities say the yen's continued weakness is due to the large interest rate differential between the US and Japan, concerns over Japan's fiscal spending, and geopolitical uncertainty. Even with official warnings from Tokyo and Washington that they are prepared to intervene again, analysts believe that the yen's depreciation pressure will persist unless there is a significant shift in the global environment or policy.

The Bank of Japan's July meeting minutes showed that inflation risks are rising, with some committee members suggesting accelerating interest rate hikes. Market expectations are for a 63% chance of a rate hike in September and almost complete pricing for a rate hike in October.
With the Obon holiday in Japan, market participation is lower and liquidity is thinner, and traders are closely watching whether the authorities will use this opportunity to intervene again.

items.title: 才要升息又得救債市？日銀陷入最尷尬處境
items.title_en: Will Raising Rates Be the Rescue for the Bond Market? BOJ Stuck in Its Most Awkward Spot
paras: 日銀 (日本央行 / BOJ) 似乎正逐步朝提前升息邁進，但高市早苗政府的擴張性財政政策推升日本公債殖利率，也讓央行面臨日益升高的政治壓力。市場憂心，即使日銀調高政策利率，貨幣緊縮效果也可能因政府要求擴大購債、壓低長期利率而遭到抵銷。
隨著政府支出計畫推高殖利率，日銀正陷入一場棘手角力：一方面希望推動貨幣政策正常化，另一方面又必須抵抗要求恢復大規模購債的聲音，而購債恰恰是央行多年來試圖逐步退出的政策。
市場對首相高市早苗擴張性財政議程的疑慮，已推升日本政府公債殖利率，增加這個已開發國家中債務負擔最沉重經濟體的融資成本。日本殖利率上升對美國公債市場造成的外溢效應，也引發華府不滿。

高市政府緊盯殖利率 施壓日銀穩定債市

高市早苗上月承諾加強與市場溝通，以維持投資人對日本財政的信心。日本媒體報導，她在 5 月與日銀總裁植田和男會面時，曾要求央行必要時增加購債，以遏止長期利率上升。
高市早苗的盟友隨後接連表達對殖利率攀升及日銀縮減資產負債表的不安。由高市親自挑選加入政府顧問小組的經濟學家永濱利廣表示，相較於升息等傳統工具，高市政府更加重視貨幣政策的「量化層面」。
同屬再通膨派的經濟產業大臣木內稔，也曾警告日銀縮減資產負債表可能衝擊經濟，並敦促決策者優先維持市場穩定。部分分析師認為，政治壓力可能已影響政策，因為日銀在 6 月升息之際，同時決定自下個會計年度起暫停縮減購債計畫。
前日銀官員愛宕伸康警告，若要求央行在長期利率上升時買進公債，反而可能引發「財政支配」疑慮，使市場懷疑日銀是否仍有能力對抗通膨。高市早苗向來支持已故前首相安倍晉三的「安倍經濟學」，其核心之一便是透過大規模資產購買刺激物價及經濟成長。

殖利率逼近 3% 日銀恐被迫再次進場

對日銀而言，重新擴大購債將與多年來退出超寬鬆政策的努力背道而馳。央行 2024 年終止殖利率曲線控制 (YCC)，並啟動縮減購債計畫，希望恢復因長期大規模干預而失去活力的債券市場。
日銀強調，只有當殖利率以脫離經濟基本面的無序方式上升，並威脅金融穩定時，才會透過緊急操作增加購債。美國財長貝森特對日本政策的關切，可能使高市政府不敢公開反對提前升息，但日銀仍在強化抵禦政治施壓的論述。
日銀上周發布研究報告指出，推升公債殖利率的主要因素是通膨升高，而非央行減少購債。6 月會議紀錄也顯示，政策委員已開始討論日銀資產負債表的最終規模，表明央行儘管面臨壓力，仍希望延續政策正常化。
然而，市場最終仍可能迫使日銀出手。日本 10 年期公債殖利率周一升至 2.805%，逐漸逼近部分分析師視為新一波賣壓觸發點的 3%。
野村證券利率策略師岩下真理表示，若日本國內投資人需求不足導致殖利率急升，日銀可能別無選擇，只能進場干預。這正是央行長期以寬鬆政策主導債券市場，如今必須付出的代價。
paras_en: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) appears to be moving step‑by‑step toward an early rate hike, but the expansionary fiscal policy of Prime Minister Kishida’s government is pushing up Japanese government‑bond yields, adding mounting political pressure on the central bank. The market worries that even if the BOJ raises its policy rate, the tightening effect could be offset by the government’s demand to expand bond purchases and keep long‑term rates low.

As government‑spending plans lift yields, the BOJ finds itself in a tricky tug‑of‑war: on one hand it wants to normalise monetary policy, on the other it must fend off calls to resume large‑scale bond buying – a policy the central bank has been trying to unwind for years.

Market scepticism about Prime Minister Kishida’s expansionary fiscal agenda has already pushed up Japanese sovereign‑bond yields, raising financing costs for the world’s most indebted advanced‑economy. The rise in Japan’s yields also creates spill‑over effects on the U.S. Treasury market, prompting displeasure in Washington.

Kishida’s administration is closely monitoring yields and pressuring the BOJ to stabilise the bond market. Kishida pledged last month to improve communication with markets to maintain investor confidence in Japan’s fiscal stance. Japanese media reported that during a May meeting with BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda, she asked the central bank to increase purchases if necessary to curb the rise in long‑term rates.

Kishida’s allies subsequently voiced concerns about climbing yields and the BOJ’s balance‑sheet reduction. Economist Toshihiro Nagahama, hand‑picked by Kishida for a government advisory panel, said the administration places more emphasis on the “quantitative” side of monetary policy than on traditional tools such as rate hikes.

Economy and Industry Minister Kenji Kawai, also a “re‑inflation” advocate, warned that a BOJ balance‑sheet shrinkage could hurt the economy and urged policymakers to prioritise market stability. Some analysts think political pressure may already be shaping policy, as the BOJ, while raising rates in June, also decided to pause its bond‑purchase tapering from the next fiscal year.

Former BOJ official Nobuyuki Atago warned that demanding the central bank buy government bonds when long‑term rates rise could raise concerns of “fiscal dominance,” causing markets to doubt the BOJ’s ability to fight inflation. Kishida has long supported the late former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe’s “Abenomics,” whose core includes massive asset purchases to spur prices and growth.

With yields approaching 3%, the BOJ may be forced to step back into the market. Re‑expanding purchases would run counter to years of effort to unwind ultra‑easy policy. The central bank ended Yield Curve Control in 2024 and began tapering purchases to revive a bond market that had lost vitality after prolonged large‑scale intervention.

The BOJ stresses it would only boost purchases in an emergency if yields rose in a disorderly way detached from economic fundamentals and threatened financial stability. U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen’s concerns about Japan’s policy may keep Kishida’s government from openly opposing an early rate hike, but the BOJ continues to reinforce its narrative of resisting political pressure.

A BOJ research paper released last week said the main driver of higher sovereign yields is rising inflation, not the central bank’s purchase reductions. Minutes from the June meeting also showed policymakers beginning to discuss the final size of the BOJ’s balance sheet, indicating that despite pressure, the bank still aims to continue normalisation.

Nevertheless, the market may ultimately force the BOJ’s hand. Japan’s 10‑year government‑bond yield rose to 2.805% on Monday, edging toward the 3% level that some analysts view as the trigger for a new wave of selling pressure.

Nomura Securities rate strategist Mari Iwashita said that if domestic investor demand falls short and yields spike sharply, the BOJ may have no choice but to intervene. That would be the price the central bank pays for having long‑run the bond market with ultra‑easy policy and now being forced to act.
